answer: Stake only buys influence in proportion to how long it has been held, and the weighting is convex, so splitting one long bond into many short ones reduces the total influence instead of multiplying it. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Call the lantern the capital, the whisper the age bonus, and the pulse the compounding curve: only undivided lantern keeps the whisper, and the pulse shows exactly how much a split loses. Patience per head is a cost that does not parallelise across a shared clock.
